title: 🎤 Part 2 — Cue Card Mastery

sections.heading: The 1-minute preparation
sections.body:
This minute is invaluable — most students waste it panicking.

Use it to:
1. Decide on ONE specific story/experience (not a general answer)
2. Note 3–4 bullet points — not full sentences
3. Think of 2 descriptive words/phrases for each bullet point
4. Plan your ending (final reflection, why it was significant)

Specific > General: "A trip to Kerala in 2019" beats "A holiday I once had".

sections.heading: Structure for 2 minutes
sections.body:
Opening (20 sec): Set the scene — when, where, who
Middle (80 sec): What happened + sensory/emotional details
Reflection (20 sec): Why it was significant + what you learned or felt

The reflection is where Band 7 becomes Band 8–9. Anyone can describe. Reflective analysis is what examiners reward.

highlight: Don't stop at 1:30. Keep talking until the examiner says "Thank you." Every extra second demonstrates fluency.

instruction: Match each speaking phrase to its function:

pairs.word: "That's an interesting question — let me think..."

explanation:
These discourse markers signal to the examiner that you're thinking in English — not translating. Using them naturally (not robotically) is a marker of Band 7+ fluency.

Key word: NATURALLY. If they sound rehearsed, they lose their effect.

title: 🗣️ Part 2 Language — Making It Flow
body:
Part 2 success = fluency + structure + specific details.

Useful language to structure your 2 minutes:

Opening: 'I\'d like to talk about... which happened/took place...'
Setting scene: 'At the time, I was... / It was a particularly...'
Main events: 'What struck me most was... / The thing I remember vividly is...'
Reflection: 'Looking back, I think... / What made it special was...'

Never just list facts. Use sensory and emotional detail.

quick.label: Sensory details ('the smell of...', 'the sound of...') score highly

question: You finish your Part 2 talk after 1 minute 20 seconds. The examiner hasn't stopped you. What should you do?
options: Continue speaking until the examiner says 'Thank you'
Start repeating what you've already said
correct: Continue speaking until the examiner says 'Thank you'
explanation:
The examiner will ALWAYS stop you at 2 minutes. If they haven't stopped you, keep going.

Stopping early signals:
❌ Running out of ideas (fluency penalty)
❌ Poor self-management

If you're worried about running out of content:
• Add more sensory/emotional detail
• Reflect on what you learned or felt
• Speculate: 'I imagine that if it had been different...'

Every extra second demonstrates fluency.
hint: The examiner controls the timing — your job is to keep talking.

question: Which Part 2 opening is Band 8?
options: 'I want to talk about my holiday.'
'The topic I have chosen is about a trip I made.'
'I\'d like to describe a journey I made to Kerala in 2019 — it was a trip that, unexpectedly, changed my perspective on what I value in travel.'
'I will now talk about a memorable travel experience from my past.'
correct: 'I\'d like to describe a journey I made to Kerala in 2019 — it was a trip that, unexpectedly, changed my perspective on what I value in travel.'
explanation:
✅ Band 8 opening:
• 'I\'d like to describe' — natural, not 'I will talk about'
• Specific: Kerala, 2019
• 'unexpectedly' — adverb adds authenticity
• 'changed my perspective on what I value in travel' — reflective, interesting claim
• Creates immediate intrigue — examiner wants to hear more

❌ Others: announce rather than engage; vague; no detail
